dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.P11Matrix
dependency_coverage.interpretation: P11Matrix n is the type of square n-by-n matrices over the exact real numbers, indexed in both directions by Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forces A, dA, Q, R, and Rinv to have the same square shape and leaves only one dimension parameter.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper has A_k, Delta A_k, and Q_k of shape m-by-k and R_k of shape k-by-k. This definition matches only the specialization m = k = n and cannot directly express the general rectangular case.

dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p11DefectCore
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is ((R^T R - A^T A) - A^T dA) - dA^T A - dA^T dA, with the subtractions associated to the left.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the complete matrix inside the two Rinv factors on the right-hand side.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: After identifying dA with Delta A_k, this is exactly E_k - A_k^T Delta A_k - (Delta A_k)^T A_k - (Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k, including all signs and the quadratic term.

dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p11Identity
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is the square matrix with real one on the diagonal and zero off the diagonal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines both the identity in hInv and the identity in the orthogonality defect.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: With Lean's n identified with the paper's k, it is the k-by-k identity required by dimensional consistency.

dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p11MatMul
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is ordinary finite matrix multiplication over the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every juxtaposed matrix product in the hypotheses, defect, residual, and conjugation is interpreted as standard matrix multiplication.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It matches the paper's products on the represented square domain. The inability to type rectangular products is caused by D001 rather than by the multiplication operation itself.

dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p11OrthogonalityDefect
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is I - Q^T Q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the left-hand side and, in particular, its sign.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper's displayed identity begins I - Q_k^T Q_k, with the same order and sign.

dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p11Transpose
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is ordinary matrix transpose, swapping row and column indices without conjugation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets Q^T, Rinv^T, A^T, dA^T, and R^T.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper works over real matrices and uses ordinary transpose, so this matches exactly.

dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p11NormalEquationResidual
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is R^T R - A^T A.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the leading term of p11DefectCore.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This has exactly the paper's sign convention E_k = R_k^T R_k - A_k^T A_k.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Lean's Eq is exact propositional equality between two values of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both hypotheses and the conclusion are exact matrix equalities, not approximate or normwise relations.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The page-312 identity is written as an exact equality and retains its quadratic residual term.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Fin n is the finite index type with n elements, conventionally represented by 0 through n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes all rows, columns, and finite matrix-product sums.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The zero-based indexing is bijectively equivalent to the paper's one-based indexing and introduces no offset into the formulas.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It selects the heterogeneous-addition operation supplied by the applicable typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: In hQR it dispatches A + dA to matrix addition.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: After instance resolution, this is the ordinary matrix sum A_k + Delta A_k used by the paper.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.add
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It equips matrices with pointwise addition inherited from their entries.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A + dA means the matrix whose entries are A_ij + dA_ij.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This is standard matrix addition and matches A_k + Delta A_k.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Nat is the type of natural numbers and includes zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The theorem quantifies over every n, including n = 0, without a positivity hypothesis.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper's identity is used for k = 1,...,n. Lean adds an empty-dimensional case not present in that range.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real is Lean's exact real-number type, not a floating-point datatype.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All matrix entries and all algebra in the proposition are exact real quantities.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper declares its matrices to be real, and the selected displayed identity is exact for the computed real-valued matrices, so the scalar semantics of the identity match.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It is exact addition of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies entrywise addition for A + dA.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It matches exact real addition in the displayed algebraic identity.

dependency_coverage.interpretation: It converts an ordinary homogeneous Add instance into the HAdd interface.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes HAdd.hAdd on two matrices return their ordinary matrix sum.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It provides a finite enumeration of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the index sum in matrix multiplication a finite sum over all n inner indices.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It selects the heterogeneous-multiplication operation supplied by a typeclass.

dependency_coverage.paper_match: After instance resolution it denotes ordinary matrix multiplication, as in the paper.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It selects the heterogeneous-subtraction operation supplied by a typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It dispatches all subtractions in the defect and residual definitions to matrix subtraction.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: After instance resolution it preserves the paper's ordered matrix differences.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Matrix m n alpha is the function type m -> n -> alpha.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Matrices and their equality are entrywise-extensional functions on row and column indices.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This is a standard faithful representation of finite matrices; the square restriction comes from D001.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.one
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It defines the identity matrix as the diagonal matrix with entry one at every diagonal position.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes p11Identity n the multiplicative identity matrix.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It matches the paper's dimensionally inferred identity matrix I.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.sub
dependency_coverage.interpretation: It equips matrices with pointwise subtraction inherited from their entries.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every matrix difference is evaluated entry by entry.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.transpose

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The verified PDF is the 2006 Numerische Mathematik article with SHA-256 72b7521848be07971a6721ea0356bb898c63e21b8ad3aa109fee8f41517284a5. PDF page 14, printed page 312, contains the cited two-line identity immediately after 'To get (7)'.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The dossier identifies HighamBench.p11_t2_orthogonality_defect_identity as the target and supplies its exact, readable, and fully explicit types.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The selected source, version, passage, and enclosing proof of Theorem 1 are correctly identified.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Printed pages 300 and 302 give A in R^{m x n}, A_k and Q_k in R^{m x k}, and R_k in R^{k x k}, with m >= n and k = 1,...,n.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: D001 makes every matrix binder a Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Real, so A, dA, Q, R, and Rinv are all n-by-n.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The target collapses the independent row and column dimensions and represents only the square specialization m = k.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 1 first fixes a full-rank input A and computed Algorithm 2 factors, assumes condition (3) for each leading R_k, and then states conclusions for k = 1,...,n.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target universally quantifies n and arbitrary A, dA, Q, R, and Rinv, subject only to hQR and hInv.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Although hQR and hInv determine dA and Rinv when the other data are fixed, the complete quantifier scope is changed from algorithm outputs and their leading blocks to arbitrary algebraic data.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper inherits m >= n, rank(A) = n, Algorithm 2 provenance, floating-point computation, condition (3), and hence nonsingularity of R_k.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean assumes only Q R = A + dA and R Rinv = I. It has no full-rank input, upper-triangularity, Algorithm 2, condition-number condition, or positive index hypothesis.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The direct residual and right-inverse assumptions are sufficient for the algebraic identity, but they do not match the hypotheses of the complete paper result.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Printed page 312 concludes with I - Q_k^T Q_k = R_k^{-T}(E_k - A_k^T Delta A_k - (Delta A_k)^T A_k - (Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k)R_k^{-1}.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The conclusion is p11OrthogonalityDefect Q = Rinv^T p11DefectCore A dA R Rinv; D002, D005, and D007 unfold it to the same expanded equality.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The final selected identity is complete and retains every correction term. The preceding Q_k formula and unexpanded middle expression are algebraically derivable from hQR, hInv, and the definitions rather than independent missing cases.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The source uses ordinary real matrix addition, subtraction, multiplication, transpose, and the k-by-k identity.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: D001-D032 resolve these operations to exact real matrices, pointwise addition and subtraction, finite row-by-column multiplication, ordinary transpose, and the diagonal identity.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: All imported operators have determinate standard meanings, and the expanded right-hand side has the source's exact order and signs. The dimensional restriction is separately recorded under S02 and S15.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Q_k and R_k are computed matrices, while Delta A_k and E_k are exactly defined residuals; the displayed identity itself has no rounding operator or approximation.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean uses exact real matrices and distinguishes dA through the exact equation Q R = A + dA; the normal-equations residual is also exact by D007.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: At the algebraic-identity level, exact operations and residual quantities are not conflated. The loss of computed provenance is instead the algorithm-linkage failure in S08.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 1 and its appendix concern leading factors produced by CGS-P, whose diagonal uses the Pythagorean formula, under condition (3).
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: No algorithm, execution trace, computed-factor predicate, leading-block relation, or CGS-P condition appears in the target.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The Lean proposition is an algorithm-independent matrix identity. That is a valid algebraic generalization, but it does not preserve the complete paper statement's algorithm linkage.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The two-line identity on printed page 312 is norm-free; the operator 2-norm appears only in the following estimate leading to equation (7).
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The Lean target contains no norm, squared norm, or componentwise error bound.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: There is no norm expression in the selected identity whose semantics could agree or disagree.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The source uses distinct m and k, takes k = 1,...,n, and uses the same k for the first k columns and the leading k-by-k factor.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean has one natural parameter n for both dimensions and permits n = 0. No leading-block index k is represented.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: No numerical constants occur in the selected identity, but its dimension and index dependence are not preserved.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Printed page 301 states the IEEE normalized-range model and a first-order convention, but printed page 312 writes the selected identity as an exact equality without fl, epsilon_M, or exceptional-value operations.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target is exact real matrix algebra and contains no floating-point model or rounding operation.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Precision and exceptional-value semantics do not operate inside this exact identity. Their missing connection to the computed factors is already assessed under S08.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The source relation is exact equality, with left side I - Q_k^T Q_k and conjugating factors R_k^{-T} on the left and R_k^{-1} on the right.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean uses Eq, the same defect sign, transpose Rinv on the left, and Rinv on the right. For finite square real matrices, hInv makes Rinv the inverse of R.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Equality direction, exactness, signs, and conjugation order match.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Delta A_k is the factorization residual Q_k R_k - A_k, and E_k is the normal-equations residual R_k^T R_k - A_k^T A_k.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: hQR is Q R = A + dA, equivalent to dA = Q R - A, while D007 defines exactly R^T R - A^T A.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The two residual notions are preserved and are not replaced by forward errors, norm bounds, or another stability notion.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The exact page-312 expansion explicitly includes -(Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k; O(epsilon_M^2) appears only in the subsequent norm estimate.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: D002 explicitly subtracts p11MatMul (p11Transpose dA) dA and the conclusion is exact Eq with no big-O remainder.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The quadratic residual term is retained exactly and no first-order truncation is applied to the identity.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The source covers rectangular m-by-k leading factors arising from CGS-P under inherited numerical hypotheses.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean specializes all matrices to square n-by-n matrices while generalizing from algorithm outputs to arbitrary matrices satisfying two algebraic equations.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: This is a mixed square specialization and algorithm-independent generalization, not an equivalent or uniformly stronger rendering of the complete paper statement.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper's full-rank setup and condition (3) are intended to produce nonsingular real factors, so the displayed inverse-based identity has a nonempty intended domain.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: For n = 1, A = 3, dA = 1, Q = 2, R = 2, and Rinv = 1/2 satisfy hQR and hInv; both sides of the conclusion equal -3.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The Lean hypotheses have nontrivial models and the conclusion is not obtained solely from an inconsistent premise or only from the empty n = 0 case.

lean_implies_paper.reasoning: Under the direct interpretation of corresponding matrices, Lean proves only the square case and contains no m-by-k matrices for m > k, no leading-block family, and no statement connecting its variables to CGS-P outputs. It therefore does not establish the complete rectangular paper result.

paper_implies_lean.reasoning: The paper's complete result concerns computed CGS-P factors under the inherited full-rank and condition-(3) context, whereas Lean quantifies over every square real tuple satisfying only hQR and hInv, including tuples that are not outputs of that algorithm and the n = 0 case.

findings.paper_evidence: A_k, Delta A_k, and Q_k are m-by-k while R_k is k-by-k, with m >= n and k = 1,...,n.
findings.lean_evidence: P11Matrix n makes all five matrix binders n-by-n and supplies no independent row dimension.
findings.impact: The theorem cannot directly state the paper's rectangular identity when m > k, so it does not cover the complete source domain.

findings.paper_evidence: The identity occurs in the proof of Theorem 1 for factors computed by Algorithm 2 under condition (3).
findings.lean_evidence: The target quantifies over arbitrary matrices constrained only by a factorization-residual equation and a right-inverse equation.
findings.impact: The Lean statement is broader algebraically but loses the computed-factor and execution-model meaning, making the complete statements incomparable rather than one simply stronger.

findings.paper_evidence: The paper applies the identity for k = 1,...,n.
findings.lean_evidence: The natural parameter n is unrestricted and therefore includes the empty 0-by-0 case.
findings.impact: An extra trivial boundary case is admitted, although nonzero nontrivial Lean instances also exist.

findings.paper_evidence: The source has I - Q_k^T Q_k and subtracts A_k^T Delta A_k, (Delta A_k)^T A_k, and (Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k inside R_k^{-T} and R_k^{-1}.
findings.lean_evidence: Unfolding p11OrthogonalityDefect, p11DefectCore, and p11NormalEquationResidual gives exactly that sign pattern, order, and quadratic term.
findings.impact: Within the square algebraic specialization, the central residual-to-defect identity itself is represented correctly.

rationale: The Lean conclusion faithfully encodes the exact expanded matrix identity on its square domain, including the normal-equations residual convention, conjugation order, defect sign, and quadratic residual product. The complete propositions are nevertheless incomparable: Lean removes the paper's CGS-P, floating-point, full-rank, condition-(3), and leading-block scope while also restricting the rectangular m-by-k matrices to square n-by-n matrices and admitting n = 0. Consequently neither complete statement implies the other under the direct correspondence, so the result is not-faithful-different.
